principles.text: When the evening watchlist review shows breakdowns everywhere — leaders rejected at the declining 9, gap-downs across groups, leader count shrinking — close the long book proactively that evening; don't wait for each individual stop to be hit.

The QUALITY of a bounce is information: off a weekly support you want it quick and strong (like crypto 2023); a bounce that hangs around the declining 50 EMA for days is failing, and repeating the pattern of the last failed cycle.

Trying to pick the turning point because you don't want to miss the reversal is paid tuition — repeated stop-outs while price goes nowhere after each stop is the market saying it's chop, not a reversal; the stop-out cluster itself is the signal to stand down.

The better a setup looks on the long side at resistance, the better it is on the short side if it fails: an inside-day 'breakout' right at the anchored VWAP from all-time highs traps breakout buyers whose stops fuel the move down — a classic failed breakout; an overshoot of the AVWAP is the ideal short scenario.
Trade what you see: if the candidate short keeps going higher without showing weakness, don't short it on the way up — wait for the failure.

Beware the laggard's tricky bounce: a name that topped BEFORE the market (made lower highs while the index made higher highs, 9<21<50 with the 50 flattening/turning down) then prints a strong-looking bounce with apparent relative strength — breaking a previous day high, reclaiming EMAs — straight into the supply range of prior red candles. That is a dead-cat bounce / bull trap, not new leadership (LITE now; OPEN January 2026). Don't buy it; when market and sector are below declining EMAs, it's a short candidate.

Judge a suspicious bounce by its FORWARD behavior, not the pattern: if the name holds above its EMAs and makes higher lows while the market makes lower lows, it graduates into a long candidate for when the market improves; if it loses the 9 (or 50) within a day or two on big red candles, the bull trap is confirmed. The pattern label matters less than how it holds up as the market weakens.

In a clear downtrend the method is still the pullback short: shorting bounces gives the highest win rate AND the best risk/reward, and keeps you moving at the same pace as the market rather than chasing breakdowns.

Track the sequential death of speculative groups as a breadth thermometer: quantum gone, nuclear gone, power generators weak, software destroyed, semi laggards breaking — when the speculative money is gone across groups, real damage has been done and a much deeper correction (e.g. QQQ to the weekly 50, ~15%) is on the table.

Range/volatility expansion near the highs on the weekly is a red flag even during an apparently healthy pullback — compare with true leaders (MU, SNDK) whose bases pull back to the weekly 9 QUIETLY, volatility contracting into the next setup rather than expanding.

The checklist to turn bullish again after de-risking: (1) breadth improves — more names showing strength and potential leadership; (2) follow-through appears after breakouts/reversals instead of instant failure; (3) your own long trades start giving positive feedback; and (4) at minimum the index reclaims its declining 9 EMA.
